name: Move Set
description: The moves a creature knows and the uses each move has left. A move is data — element, power, accuracy, priority, targeting and optional effect payload — while the set is per-creature state: which of those moves are known and their remaining power points. This component validates a selection and spends a use only when combat.command_round commits it, so a cancelled or still-collecting round cannot drain PP. It deliberately owns neither turn order nor damage: command_round compares priority and speed, combat.type_chart answers effectiveness, and combat.damage_resolver owns the final number. Keeping those seams separate lets the same move catalog serve creature battles, tactical RPGs and cooldown-free ability systems.

inputs.name: moveCatalog
inputs.description: Move definitions keyed by id: element, power, accuracy, priority, target rule, maximum PP and optional status-effect payload.

inputs.name: knownMoves
inputs.description: Per-creature move ids and current PP. This is state supplied by the host or restored save, not a second species catalog.

inputs.name: maxMovesPerCreature
inputs.description: Known-move cap. Four matches the reference genre's compact decision set; other games can raise or remove the pressure.

inputs.name: fallbackMoveId
inputs.description: Optional move available when every known move is exhausted. Omit it to reject actions until the creature switches or uses an item.

outputs.name: availableMoves
outputs.description: Known moves with current and maximum PP, including whether each can presently be selected.

outputs.name: lastSelection
outputs.description: The validated creature, move and selection metadata handed to the command round.

provenance: Added 2026-11-02 for the Pokémon battle-and-capture extraction. Searched the combat catalog first: combat.hotbar_abilities owns cooldown-based activation, combat.tactical_attack resolves a grid shot, and combat.action_point_economy budgets a whole turn; none owns a creature's known moves or per-move PP. Library-native; this is move data and PP state, not a second attack resolver or turn queue.
